title: Beijing: A Culinary Memory
text:
A list of food memories back in Beijing. Always updating…
蒋姨家的饺子是全世界最好吃的东西！ 
京华楼的油爆双脆是中餐集刀工，火候，调味于一体的典范。 
俏东北的东北名菜锅包肉。 
德富来炒菜店的火爆鳝鱼，双椒肥肠, 板前川菜，镬气十足。 
京华楼姑苏“四大名肉”之糟汁肉：选用上好的五花肉蒸至定型，用酒糟泥包裹腌制两天，再经过油炸、糟汁炖、冷却，最后上桌前蒸熟浇汁，糟香浓郁、软糯鲜香。 
潮上潮的乳鸽，外皮酥脆，肉质爆汁。 
丰泽园的葱烧海参，葱香浓郁，海参软糯入味。 
湘上湘的东安鸡，味型独特，醋酸与姜辣交织，回味悠长。

title: Reale: ‘The complexity of ingredients’
text:
The natural flavour from ingredients are generally more complex and deep than what seasonings can provide. Great chefs bring out the best in each ingredient, but Chef Romito takes it to another level. He uses all kinds of techniques to showcase multiple flavors from a single ingredient in each dish. Over ~80% of dishes have some aspects that I’ve never tasted before, and ~80% is pretty easy for me to enjoy.
I also want to give a big shout out to the manager, Cristiana Romito, who is the sister of Chef Romito. Being the only non-Italian-speaking table at that lunch service, I can see that the chef tried to avoid talking to us because he only speaks a little English. The manager (or more importantly, as the chef’s sister), ‘solicited’ him to chat with us and graciously helped us understand each other. We had a wonderful conversation about his unique cooking techniques and his overall culinary philosophy. It was truly a revelation for me to realize how hospitality can transform a dining experience into something truly memorable.
I think all the dishes are well-designed and well-executed. Any dishes lower than 8/10 are just because I’m not used to that flavour profile. Sometimes great flavours are hidden behind unpleasant smells/tastes, like cheese and century-age eggs. You just need to learn how to appreciate them.
This resatrant has a heavy focus on vegetables, but it’s not bacause of veganism or vegetarianism. The chef is just trying to showcase the complexity of ingredients, and vegetables are more complex than meat. I think this is the way for a more sustainable future, and I hope more chefs will follow this path instead of forbidding meat.
Mixed wild greens with tomato, extra virgin olive oil and spelt 8/10 The greens are from the restaurant’s garden, with some umami elements in the dressing.



Mixed wild greens


Ostrica e cicoria 7/10 It’s a fresh taste of bitterness and brininess.



Ostrica e cicoria


Rice, basil pesto, anise and lemon 7/10 They emphasised that it’s not a risotto. The lemon and pesto are balanced with the sweetness from anise, but the taste of anise (other than sweetness) is a bit too strong for me.



Rice, basil pesto, anise and lemon


Bread 9/10 A simple sourdough bread that is meant to be enjoyed alone. The chef and manager’s parents used to run a bakery when they were young.
Tomato and watermelon 10/10 The watermelon was dehydrated, then rehydrated to be infused with tomato flavours. The texture of watermelon is really unique.



Tomato and watermelon, and bread behind


Codfish and fig leaf 10/10 The fish is cooked to perfection, with the unique taste of fig leaf made into a smooth sesame sause-like consistency.



Codfish and fig leaf


Warm Swiss chard salad 10/10 The swiss chard is cooked in different ways like fried, blanched, pickled, etc., then mixed together to show how a simple vegetable can taste so diverse.



Warm Swiss chard salad


Carrot 10/10 This is my favourite dish, because the fermented carrot juice at the bottom is so good. The sourness from fermentation and sweetness from fresh carrots are balanced just at the right point.



Carrot


Duck and juniper 9/10 The duck is first roasted in oven as a whole bird, then ice-bathed to stop cooking (first time I’ve heard it used on roasted meat). Then the breast is filleted and finished on a grill. I do want to give this technique a try back home.



Duck and juniper


Penne and sage 8/10 The penne is al dente with a sage sauce full of bitterness. The waiter told us we’ll be able to appreciate the taste of bitterness after several bites. I feel like I tasted something in the last one or two pasta, but still the strong bitterness won’t go away. The soup is also made with sage, but less bitter and more refreshing. The small leaf in the soup is meant to be eaten at the end, and it’s a sweet leaf that the taste lasted for hours in my mouth.



Penne and sage


Red pepper and bread 9/10 It’s a fried bread dough soaked with red pepper sauce/juice. The texture is almost steak-like: a crust on the outside with a soft inside. Despite the lack of meat dishes for the whole meal, I still feel fulfilled at the end.



Red pepper and bread


Apricot, rosemary and rhubarb 6/10 Over half of the main desert I had in Europe this summer is made with apricot, so this one didn’t stand out. The apricot itself is not flavorful compared to others, and I personally do not like rhubarb.



Apricot, rosemary and rhubarb


Petit four 8/10 A melon with spice, like the Mexican fruit cut, some cheese, and a chocolate sorbet (a really good one).



Petit four

title: About me
text:
I am a computational biologist interested in understanding how changes in RNA and protein sequences produce differences in molecular structure, stability, and disease biology.
I am currently completing my Ph.D. in the Korkin Lab at Worcester Polytechnic Institute. My work spans bioinformatics, machine learning, protein structure, and molecular dynamics.

title: Senbao Lu
text:
I am a Ph.D. candidate in the Korkin Lab at Worcester Polytechnic Institute. My research combines bioinformatics, machine learning, and structural biology to understand how alternative splicing affects protein stability and disease.
I develop computational methods for analyzing protein isoforms and validate their predictions using structural, evolutionary, and experimental evidence.

title: Research
section: Molecular dynamics and protein thermal stability
text:
Molecular dynamics and protein thermal stability



Molecular-dynamics workflow



Question
Can molecular-dynamics simulations reveal how sequence variation influences protein thermal stability?


Approach
I compare structural behavior across simulation temperatures using measures such as conformational fluctuation, compactness, and secondary-structure retention.


Significance
The project connects experimental stability measurements with atomistic descriptions of protein behavior.

title: Vandelvira: ‘Genius cuisine’
text:
Baeza, a quaint city about half an hour’s drive north of Jaén, is home to Chef Juan Carlos García’s family-owned convent. In 2022, he reopened this historic establishment into a restaurant, and his culinary creations have been nothing short of remarkable. The food here reminded me of Reale *** in Italy, and it’s no coincidence that Chef García has been collaborating with the renowned chef Niko Romito this year to explore the complexities of bitterness. I want to use the term ‘genius cuisine’ to describe their food, a feeling that I did not get anywhere else, not noma, not Plénitude.
Chef García’s dishes are bold, innovative, and occasionally challenging, but in a delightful way. The service is impeccable, in sync, yet infused with warmth and genuine hospitality. I firmly believe that this restaurant is on a rapid ascent towards earning more Michelin stars. Here are a few of my personal favorites from my recent visit (my absolute favorites are 1, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11):
P1 Squid and Iberian ham: thinly sliced squid and ham with ham dashi. The texture of squid and ham complements with each other, and the fat from ham enhanced the squid flavor. The dashi is full of aging flavors.



Squid and Iberian ham


P2 Chard, licorice beurre blanc: this is the first of three licorice courses, with the strongest licorice flavor. I personally do not like licorice that much, but the contrast of sweet and bitterness from chard is very interesting.



Chard, licorice beurre blanc


P3 Green peppers, caviar and licorice: this one is more complex with acidity from pickling the pepper, a slight spiciness from pepper, savory from both pickling and caviar, and the sweetness from licorice. I prefer this one to the previous one because it’s more balanced.



Green peppers, caviar and licorice


P4 Shrimp and licorice: this one is my favorite one among the three. The shrimp is cooked tableside with 90oC sea water pouring on it. The added sweet liquor to the head of shrimp reminded me a classical combination of Shaoxing wine and raw shrimp in Chinese cuisine.



Shrimp and licorice





Shrimp being cooked tableside


P5 White Asparagus: the pickled asparagus is bright, refreshing, and crisp. Great transition to the heavier dishes.



White Asparagus


P6 White anchovy and anchovy sauce: the sauce is creamy and full of umami flavor. The texture of the white anchovy is insane: I thought it was cured extensively because of its gelatinous texture, however, they told me it was only cured in salt for 6 minutes.



White anchovy and anchovy sauce


P7 kaki and trout: another fascinating combination between Hachiya persimmon and trout roe. The sweetness and a hint of tanginess from the fruit really highlighted the savory and ocean flavor in the trout roe. My only critic is that they put too much roe.



kaki and trout


P8 Green peas and “butifarra”: I really like the complex pork fatty flavor and texture from this Catalan sausage. I think they might also blend in sticky rice. The added truffle is from a local mountain where the farmer started to spread truffle spore 16 years ago and only be able to start harvesting recently.



Green peas and “butifarra”


P9 Rabbit: rabbit skewer on rosemary and rabbit brain. Great semi glaze.



Rabbit


P10 Black mole and blood sausage: another very complex dish with spiciness, bitterness, savory. It tastes like putting a churro without sugar or cinnamon into Mexican black bean stew.



Black mole and blood sausage


P11 White radish, ham toffee, and Maritozzo: I’m not sure if this is mean to be a desert, but if it is, then it’s my favorite desert for the recent years! The radish is so tender and absorbed all flavors from the ham, kind of like a high-end Japanese Oden. The Iberian ham and truffle work very well with the radish.



White radish, ham toffee, and Maritozzo


P12 Caramelized egg custard and peppers: interesting texture with a bit raw egg taste.



Caramelized egg custard and peppers


P13 Piquillo peppers, black pepper and chocolate: It’s not my first time to have pepper with chocolate, but it still surprised me.



Piquillo peppers, black pepper and chocolate


P14 Canelé, chocolate and ginger: great canelé, firm outside, soft inside.



Canelé, chocolate and ginger
